newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo government to nationalise TV station.
newsitem.headline: New Congo government to nationalise TV station.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's month-old government in the Democratic Republic of Congo intends to nationalise a popular private television station and impose hefty taxes on other private media, state radio announced on Tuesday.
"Tele Kin Malebo will be nationalised and become the second chain of the Television of the People," the radio said.

There are five private television stations broadcasting in Kinshasa, of which Tele Kin Malebo is one of the most popular, and four private radios in the capital as well as numerous church radios across the vast Central African country.

"The minister of information wants a percentage of the takings from private television and radio stations to enter the public treasury, 40 percent for non-religious stations and 20 percent for radio stations Elykia and Sango Mala (Church radios)," state radio said.

The decision of one-time Maoist Kabila's government to slap a private management contract for railways in the South and East of the country has already raised concerns in business circles over his stated commitment to encouraging private investment.

Privately owned media began to flourish in the former Zaire after former dictator President Mobutu Sese Seko opened Africa's third largest country to democratic reforms in 1990 and allowed a free press.

Tele Kin Malebo, the one station which will be fully nationalised according to the announcement, belonged to a former ally of Mobutu -- who was ousted last month after a seven month rebel campaign by Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo.
The director of the National Radio and Television of Congo (RTNC) justified the seizure of the station's equipment by saying it had been bought with money stolen from the state.

"For the stations belonging to dignitaries of the former regime, the equipment was originally ordered for state media. Since they diverted this equipment we are now returning it to the people," Jose Kajangua, the new director of the national radio and television explained in an interview on state television.
Kabila's government banned advertising, the main source of revenue for private media in the new Congo, in the first week after taking power.
